title: What Is OAuth?
topic: What is OAuth? — how OAuth 2.0 delegated authorization actually works: the four roles, the authorization code flow with PKCE, tokens and scopes, the other grant types, security pitfalls and RFC 9700 best current practice, building and debugging real integrations, and how OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.1 fit on top.

concepts.title: Why OAuth Exists
concepts.brief: The problem OAuth solves: password sharing, delegated access, modern app integrations. Authentication vs authorization. Real-world examples: logging into a third-party app, connecting GitHub, linking Google Calendar. The cast of characters: resource owner, client, authorization server, resource server. What the reader should understand before moving on.

concepts.title: The OAuth Mental Model
concepts.brief: How the flow works at a high level. Access tokens, refresh tokens, scopes, consent screens. Why OAuth uses redirects instead of handing credentials to apps. The basic sequence of events. A diagram-driven explanation of request, approval, token exchange, and API access.

concepts.title: Tokens Up Close
concepts.brief: What a token actually is: opaque vs JWT access tokens (RFC 9068), bearer semantics (RFC 6750), audience and resource indicators (RFC 8707), introspection (RFC 7662) and revocation (RFC 7009), expiry and refresh, discovery metadata (RFC 8414) and JWKS. How a resource server validates a token, and the trade-off between local JWT validation and calling introspection.

concepts.title: OAuth 2.0 Flows in Practice
concepts.brief: Authorization Code flow as the default pattern. PKCE and why it matters for mobile and browser-based apps. Client Credentials for machine-to-machine. Device Code for input-constrained devices. Implicit flow and why it is discouraged now. Which flow to pick, by client type.

concepts.title: Security, Pitfalls, and Best Practices
concepts.brief: Common mistakes: leaked tokens, weak redirect URI validation, poor scope design. Token storage for web, mobile, and server-side. CSRF, the state parameter, mix-up attacks and iss, replay risks. Refresh token rotation and revocation. RFC 9700 best current practice, DPoP and mTLS sender-constraining. How to think about OAuth securely in real systems.

concepts.title: Building and Using OAuth Systems
concepts.brief: Implementing an OAuth client step by step. How an authorization server works internally at a practical level. Testing OAuth integrations. Debugging common failures and understanding error responses (invalid_grant, invalid_client, redirect_uri_mismatch, invalid_scope). A build-or-buy trade-off at the end.

concepts.title: OpenID Connect and the Road to OAuth 2.1
concepts.brief: OpenID Connect as the identity layer on top of OAuth: id_token, the openid scope, nonce, UserInfo, discovery. What OAuth 2.1 consolidates and removes. Where OAuth is heading — token exchange, identity chaining, and authorization for AI agents.

notes: Filed as a book request with a 5-chapter outline; chapters kept as the five user concepts, with two added chapters (tokens up close, OIDC/OAuth 2.1) to cover the token anatomy and identity layer the outline referenced but did not give room to.
